documents.title: A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.
documents.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a major determinant of poor prognosis in systemic lupus erythematosus, yet reliable tools for early identification of unfavorable renal outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to identify early prognostic factors for complete renal response (CRR) at 12 months in active LN and to develop interpretable machine learning (ML) models for early prediction of treatment response. In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML mode

documents.title: Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis.
documents.abstract: Inflammatory diseases consist of a diverse group of conditions characterized by immune responses leading to inflammation causing damage and abnormality in function. Atopic dermatitis (AD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) both exhibit aberrant Th2 cell activity, leading to epithelial barrier dysfunction in the skin and gut, respectively. Although both diseases share similar features, differences in their tissue-specific pathology, clinical manifestations, and immune profiles may provide valuable insights into the distinct mechanisms underlying each disease.

documents.title: A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.
documents.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with substantial global mortality. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have shown promise for mortality prediction, evidence focused specifically on critically ill patients remains limited. In addition, meaningful clinical implementation requires models that rely on a minimal set of readily available variables to enable rapid risk stratification. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based model for predicting mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with an emphasis

documents.title: Deep-Learning Analysis of Peripheral Blood Smear for Prediction of Acute Inflammatory States and Chronic Comorbidities: Development and Internal Validation Study.
documents.abstract: Peripheral blood smear (PBS) examination provides morphological information on immune cells that reflects systemic pathophysiology, yet whether it can be used to predict systemic states has not been systematically established.

documents.title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.
documents.abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis-regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors pro

documents.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
documents.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) i

documents.title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.
documents.abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning-based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog-aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence-based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning-based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize

documents.title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.
documents.abstract: Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes-fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns-were incorporated into a stacked machine

documents.title: Interpretable machine learning applied to high-dimensional salivary proteomics in pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases.
documents.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), including Crohn's disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), and inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBD-U), are chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. Current methods for classification and longitudinal monitoring are invasive, expensive, and often delayed, limiting timely diagnosis and management. This proof-of-concept study reports the first application of high-dimensional salivary proteomics integrated with interpretable artificial intelligence/machine learning (ML) to define a minimal protein signature for pediatric IBD classific

documents.title: FlexENN: A Graph Neural Network for Binding Energy Prediction of Globular and Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.
documents.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) drive a large fraction of cellular signaling, transcription, and assembly through interfaces that often lack a defined geometry, making the prediction of their binding energies challenging for methods developed primarily for folded complexes. Here, we introduce FlexENN, an interface-focused message-passing graph neural network framework comprising two independently trained models: FlexENN-F for folded protein complexes and FlexENN-I for complexes containing a disordered partner. The FlexENN architecture constructs a local interface graph in which each r
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.
documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entering obstetrics and prenatal medicine, particularly in prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal magnetic resonance imaging, genomic screening, risk prediction and clinical decision support. The aim of this review was to summarize current evidence, recent developments and implementation requirements for AI-based applications in prenatal care.

documents.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.
documents.abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid populati

documents.title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models Incorporating TGFBIp Expression for Prognosis Prediction in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer.
documents.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for diverse prognostic tools. Transforming growth factor-β-induced protein (TGFBIp) has been implicated in ovarian cancer progression, but its incremental prognostic value within machine learning frameworks remains unexplored.

documents.title: Metabolic Profiling Combined With Machine Learning for Assessing Clonal Hematopoiesis Status in Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: An Exploratory Analysis.
documents.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has emerged as a potential contributor to the pathogenesis of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), yet the clinical and metabolic features of ITP patients harboring CH-associated mutations remain poorly characterized. We retrospectively analyzed a genomic discovery cohort of 1817 patients with chronic ITP, identifying CH in 196 individuals (10.8%), with DNMT3A as the most frequently mutated gene. In a metabolomic profiling cohort of 539 patients (492 ITP-non-CH, 47 ITP-CH), we characterized plasma metabolic signatures using untargeted LC-MS/MS and systematically evaluated t

documents.title: Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to investigate clinical correlates of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults, compare seven classification models, and interpret the selected gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier. This single-center observational study included 572 adults reported to be aged ≥ 60 years who received care between June 2021 and June 2023, comprising 385 participants classified as having persistent AF and 187 comparators. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) were used for candidate-variable assessment and f

documents.title: Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.
documents.abstract: Computational methods are increasingly applied to the discovery of plant-derived peptides, but the extent, composition and reporting practice of this literature have not been mapped. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed were searched for records published between 2021 and 2026. Of 5062 unique records, 593 were screened at title and abstract, 88 full texts were assessed, 80 sources met all five eligibility criteria and 79 were charted. Overall, 49 (62.0%) were primary studies, 12 (15.2%) described a tool or database and 18 (

documents.title: Integrating large-scale serum baseline metabolomics and APOE ε4 genotype status for the non-invasive detection of Alzheimer's disease in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.
documents.abstract: Accurate Alzheimer's disease (AD) detection remains challenging and often requires invasive or costly procedures. Blood-based metabolomic signatures offer a promising non-invasive comparative approach for disease stratification. This study aimed to evaluate whether large-scale serum metabolite panel combined with apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 genotype status could distinguish AD from cognitively normal (CN) individuals within the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.

documents.title: Machine learning for host-pathogen protein-protein interaction prediction: A tutorial paper.
documents.abstract: The study of Host-Pathogen Protein-Protein Interactions (HP-PPIs) is critical for understanding mechanisms of infectious disease and for the development of therapeutic interventions. Computational prediction of HP-PPIs has become essential due to the limitations of experimental approaches, which are labour-intensive and expensive. In this tutorial, we present a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for HP-PPI prediction implemented in Google Colab. The workflow consists of six stages implemented in six Google Colab notebooks: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, machin

documents.title: SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling.
documents.abstract: Accurate battery modeling is essential for reliable state estimation in modern applications, such as predicting the remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy in battery management systems. Existing approaches face several limitations: model-based methods require a large number of physical parameters; data-driven methods rely heavily on labeled datasets; and current physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often lack aging adaptation, still depend on many physical parameters, or require continuous state regeneration. In this work, we propose SeqBattNet, a discrete-state PINN with

documents.title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer's Disease.
documents.abstract: The gut microbiota-immune-metabolism axis has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis; however, the key host molecular targets linking peripheral dysregulation to central neurodegeneration remain elusive.

documents.title: Screening of oxidative stress-related signature genes and construction of an interpretable discriminant model for preeclampsia.
documents.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy complication threatening maternal and fetal health, and its onset and progression are closely associated with placental oxidative stress. However, a systematic understanding of oxidative stress-related genes in PE and their roles in immune regulation remains lacking.

documents.title: A multisource clinical deep learning model for early identification of mental disorders in first-visit psychiatric patients.
documents.abstract: Mental disorders often present with overlapping symptoms at the first psychiatric visit, making early identification difficult. This study included 5802 first-visit psychiatric patients and developed a TUCH-FT for multi-label classification of mental disorders using demographic information, clinical history, and item-level Symptom Checklist-90 data. Final diagnostic labels were determined through longitudinal follow-up, treatment response, and psychiatric expert evaluation. The original FT-Transformer places heterogeneous clinical variables in a single sequence, which may weaken source-specifi

documents.title: An interpretable machine learning model using routine clinical indicators for early pediatric sepsis risk stratification: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
documents.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide. The 2024 Phoenix Sepsis Criteria emphasize early recognition of organ dysfunction. Conventional diagnostics like blood cultures are time-consuming, and existing machine learning models lack early pathogen-level classification. A machine learning framework for early pediatric sepsis warning and Gram-stain pathogen classification was developed and validated using routine clinical indicators.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

documents.title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure.
documents.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by complex pathophysiological processes including abnormal mechanical stress and immune microenvironment remodeling. Although mechanical stimulus is known to trigger maladaptive cardiac remodeling, the systematic role of mechanical stimulus-related genes (MSRGs) in HF diagnosis and immune modulation remains poorly defined. This study aims to identify MSRG-based diagnostic biomarkers, characterize molecular subtypes, and explore their cellular localization and immune microenvironment interactions in HF.

documents.title: Development of a Machine-Learning Model for Strongyloidiasis Risk Stratification in Migrant Populations.
documents.abstract: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection with the potential for fatal hyperinfection, underscoring the need for screening strategies. A machine-learning model was developed and externally validated to support strongyloidiasis risk stratification among migrants from endemic areas.
documents.journal: Research and reports in tropical medicine

documents.title: A lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for Kazakh Sign Language recognition under signer-independent conditions.
documents.abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) in low-resource sign languages is still limited due to the lack of annotated data, high variability of signers, and lack of benchmarks; Kazakh Sign Language (KzSL) is a representative example of such a low-resource language. The proposed research introduces a novel method for isolated KzSL recognition based on a purpose-collected dataset of RGB video streams of five signers, represented by 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, facial, and hand landmark vectors extracted using MediaPipe Holistic. The final dataset consists of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 output c

documents.title: SelCysML: a hybrid ML-BLAST pipeline for the automated identification and functional annotation of bacterial selenoproteins.
documents.abstract: Selenoproteins are characterized by the incorporation of selenocysteine (Sec) via UGA codon recoding, play vital roles in redox homeostasis and enzymatic catalysis. Despite this biological significance, their computational identification remains challenging, and recent assessments confirm that public databases suffer from widespread annotation errors, often misclassifying these proteins. Current predictive tools frequently operate as "black boxes" with limited interpretability or lack integrated functional validation layers, which contributes to high false-positive rates and persistent ambigui

documents.title: Dietary amino acid composition and elevated fasting glucose in children and adolescents from four Chinese provinces: a cross-sectional study combining regression and machine learning.
documents.abstract: Using an integrated analytical pipeline that combines regression and machine learning, with nonlinear dose-response modeling, this cross-sectional study sought to examine dietary amino acid composition in relation to elevated fasting glucose (EFG) in children and adolescents.

documents.title: A reproducible open-data framework for interpretable breast cancer diagnosis and cytopathology education.
documents.abstract: Quantitative nuclear morphology links cytopathological assessment with interpretable diagnostic modeling and provides a practical foundation for teaching medical artificial intelligence. This study evaluated a reproducible framework that connects nuclear feature interpretation, malignant-versus-benign classification, and evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.
